- **`access-security.crud-permission-matrix`** (was pin-only) → **live**: built 3 objects + 3 permission sets + 3 server-proven personas and drove the full 36-cell CRUD grid — allow 15/15 succeed+persist, deny 21/21 `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, denied-CREATE leaves 0 rows; viewAllRecords/modifyAllRecords both-sides pass. **0 fail-open cells, no cross-persona leak.** (clause 5 guest-lane still `blocked(fixture)`.)
- **`access-security.permission-matrix-edit-loop`** partial → **pass**: the console PermissionMatrixEditor (clause 5) now driven live — checkbox toggle → `PUT /meta/permission/...` → server-truth re-read confirms the verb flipped.
- **`studio-authoring.permission-matrix-editor-ux`** blocked → **partial (live)**: editor reachable and functional (field-filter, read-only badge, narrow-viewport bulk column); B4 bulk-over-visible `blocked(environment)`.
- **`access-security.capability-declaration-lifecycle`** blocked → **partial (live)**: `sys_capability` DECLARE (data door) + shadow-name guard (platform names 403) + write-door validation + GRANT side all live; REQUIRE-side `blocked(fixture)` (no runtime-drivable capability-gated action; platform system-cap gates key off positions/isPlatformAdmin, so a set-held cap is fail-safe refused).

Revised totals: **40 PASS / 89 PARTIAL / 5 FAIL / 80 BLOCKED / 1 NOT-RUN** (judged 214/215; title unchanged).

**Observation (fail-safe, not filed):** the console permission-matrix editor writes the `meta/permission` projection, but live enforcement resolves from `sys_permission_set` data rows — so an editor save did not flip a data-row-backed persona's access on this EE image (runtime-created sets also resolve read-only in the editor). It is fail-safe (never fail-open), but "editor edits don't reach enforcement" is a two-store-consistency question worth a maintainer look; not filed pending that call.

**Approvals (was 1 PASS / 11 BLOCKED on the cluster → 12/12 PASS live-UI):** inbox render + drawer actions, per-group signoff (server-computed chips reconciled at each stage), viewer-gating (both sides — non-approver drawer omits Approve/Reject, forged approve → 403), notification deep-link (cold-load opens the right drawer), the 9-way decision-action matrix (approve/reject/reassign/revise/resubmit/maxRevisions-auto-reject/recall/remind/request-info), decision-only-via-service (forged resume → 403, owner service → completed), dynamic approver routing (typed record-picker, staged), OOO delegation reroute (+audit +notif +expiry), record-page decisions (locked exec vs editable manager, single reject dialog — no #3126 double), setup nav order, pending-count badge clamp ("9+" badge / unclamped popover). No defects.

**Dashboards / charts / reports (was 1 PASS / 5 PARTIAL / 4 BLOCKED → 6 PASS / 3 PARTIAL / 1 BLOCKED live-UI):** charts actually paint — recharts SVG with real geometry (treemap 5 nested rects, sankey 5 flow links, scatter 6 points, combo dual-axis), mark counts equal the analytics buckets; chart-type-matrix all 16 families; strict-widget author-time rejection (12 stray-key variants → 422); dataset-report designer draft→publish→auto-flow render; system-overview live counts reconciled; cube-query reconciled bucket-for-bucket. Partials: global-filters-rescope (runtime clauses pass; only the Studio widget-inspector authoring round-trip not driven), drill-through-range and empty-null-bucket (month-bucket UI path blocked by the analytics defect below). Blocked: `saved-report-ownership` — the saved-reports **service** (`/api/v1/reports*`) returns 501 "not configured" **on the showcase dev app too**, not just EE — the `sys_saved_report` service is a separate plugin absent in both; the `/meta/report` metadata reports render fine. **New defect extracted:** #13714 — analytics cube query with a `timeDimensions` month granularity on a date dimension crashes `500 DATABASE_ERROR` (count/status buckets fine); this is what blocks the month-bucket UI drill/empty-state clauses above.

Net: the three subsystems the maintainer asked to test (reports/approvals/charts) are now UI-verified end-to-end on the environment that actually carries them; the cluster's blocked verdicts for these stand as "not mounted on the EE image" (a deployment-shape fact), now paired with live-UI PASS on the composed showcase app.

Cluster-mode test matrix — the coordination / data-integrity / topology concerns that the feature checklist doesn't cover, run directly against the live 3-replica EE deployment (Traefik + redis cluster driver), driving replicas individually via `docker exec` to control which node handles each request.

**Coordination primitives / data integrity across replicas**
- **Autonumber counter** — 60 concurrent creates spread across all 3 replicas → 60 distinct `autonumber` values, **no collision**. (The `#8686` seed warning about two counters is a seed/API tenancy split, not a cross-replica race; the cross-replica counter is coordinated.) ✅
- **Unique constraint** — same value inserted concurrently on all 3 replicas → exactly **1 × 201 / 2 × 409**, one row persisted. ✅
- **Concurrent write durability** (from the load harness) — 200 concurrent creates → 200 persisted, 200 distinct, no lost writes / dupes; 30 concurrent unguarded PATCH to one record → row consistent, one winner. ✅
- **OCC across replicas** — broken, tracked as objectstack#13382 (Postgres token format). 🔴

**Metadata / cache coherence**
- **Existing-object update propagation** — a label change on app-2 is visible on app-3 and app-4 (metadata.changed pubsub fans out). ✅ — contrast with #13331, where a *newly authored* object's ObjectQL engine registration is replica-local (2/3 hard-404 through the LB under load; severity quantified on #13331).

**Session / authz across replicas**
- **Session revocation** — after `POST /auth/sign-out` on app-2, the token is rejected on all 3 replicas (DB-backed sessions). ✅ (First reading was a test artifact — sign-out needs a JSON body or returns 400; with `{}` it revokes cluster-wide.)
- **Authz grants cache** — `OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS` is unset (0) → cache off → no revocation-staleness window; permission edits take effect immediately (matches the permission-matrix edit-loop live result). ✅ (safe by default)

**Topology / availability**
- **Replica kill + recover** — `docker stop app-4` during load → LB served 30/30 200 (Traefik routed to survivors), data readable, app-4 rejoined in ~15s. ✅
- **Rolling restart drain** — 60/60 probes through a one-replica restart under Traefik readiness health-checks (earlier). ✅
- **Split-brain guard** — a boot with `OS_CLUSTER_DRIVER=memory` + `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS=2` **refuses to start** (`✗ ClusterServicePlugin: multi-node deployment declared … driver is in-process "memory" … split-brain`, exit 1), override `OS_ALLOW_MEMORY_CLUSTER_MULTINODE=true`. ✅
- **Leader failover / job continuity** — a per-minute schedule flow fired **exactly once per minute across a mid-window `docker stop` of a replica** (the killed minute and the recovery minute each = 1 row, no miss, no double). The per-tick `cluster.lock` acquisition gives inherent failover. ✅
- **Stuck-datasource readiness** — a datasource with an unstartable driver 503s `/ready` cluster-wide and isn't evicted on delete → LB drains everything; tracked as objectstack#13408. 🔴
- **Licensed node-cap advisory** — the documented `cluster.mdx §8` advisory never fires because the EE gate returns no `admitted`; the license `maxNodes` is inert. Filed as **objectstack-ai/cloud#1824**. 🟠

**Documented non-goals (verified, not defects)**
- Cross-node realtime fan-out is a documented non-goal (`cluster.mdx §3`); the EE image does not mount a realtime HTTP surface (`/realtime`, `/events` → 404). Recorded.

Net cluster-mode posture: coordination (locks/counters/unique/leader-failover), org isolation, session/permission propagation, and HA (node loss, rolling restart, split-brain refusal) all hold; the open gaps are the three already-tracked defects (#13331 runtime-metadata registration, #13382 OCC, #13408 readiness) plus the inert node-cap (cloud#1824). All test fixtures cleaned up; cluster left healthy.

Cluster load/stress test — ramped to saturation against the live 3-replica EE deployment (Traefik LB, redis driver, Postgres 16 `max_connections=200`), sampling DB connections + `/ready` every 5s.

**P1 — `/health` (process-only, no DB), 8s/step:** clean to saturation.
| conc | rps | err% | p50 | p95 | p99 | max |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 25 | 973 | 0 | 20 | 64 | 102 | 333 |
| 100 | 1051 | 0 | 80 | 187 | 349 | 2695 |
| 400 | 1376 | 0 | 197 | 405 | 3631 | 8050 |

The HTTP / Traefik / Node layer sustains ~1,000–1,400 rps of trivial requests with 0 errors — the front door is not the bottleneck.

**P2 — authed `GET /data/note?limit=10` (org-scoped, DB), 8s/step:** this is the ceiling.
| conc | rps | err% | p50 | p95 | p99 |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 | 19 | 0 | 513 | 813 | 1016 |
| 50 | 24 | 0 | 1988 | 2485 | 2627 |
| 100 | 25 | 0 | 3738 | 4584 | 5141 |
| 150 | — | **77.8%** | — | 12027 | 12834 (**1070× 503**) |

Throughput plateaus at **~25 rps** across the whole cluster while latency climbs linearly with concurrency (classic closed-system saturation: throughput flat ⇒ latency = concurrency ÷ throughput). At conc=150 the app sheds load — 78% `503` — rather than queueing unbounded.

**P3 — `POST /data/note` create, 8s/step:** same **~25 rps** write ceiling, 0 errors to conc=80, p50 446ms→2638ms.

**P4 — sustained 45s @ conc=50 (80/20 read/write):** 27 rps, 0 errors, p50 1746ms / p95 2638ms — **stable, no drift or degradation over the window** (no memory-creep collapse, no readiness flap).

**Root cause of the ~25 rps ceiling — the default DB connection pool, not Postgres.** Throughout every phase the sampler showed Postgres holding only **~9–21 connections against its 200 limit**, and at steady state the app accounts for just **9 connections total across 3 replicas (~3 per replica)**. No `OS_*`/pool-size env is set on this deployment, so the pg driver's small default pool is in force: ~3 concurrent DB ops per replica × 3 replicas ÷ ~350ms/query ≈ the 25 rps observed. The DB has ~10× headroom that the pool never uses.

**Takeaways for a cluster deployment:**
1. Authed data-API throughput is pool-bound at ~25 rps by default and scales with replica count, not with the (idle) DB headroom — raising the per-replica connection pool is the lever, but no documented `OS_*` knob exposes it on this image (worth surfacing one).
2. Under a concurrency spike (≥~150) the data path sheds to `503` rather than degrading gracefully; combined with Traefik readiness-draining, a sustained spike risks the whole-fleet-drain failure mode already seen with the stuck-datasource case (#13408). Front-door (`/health`, static) capacity is ~1,400 rps and is not the constraint.

No data corruption or lost writes at any load level (the concurrency-integrity tests above cover that); this phase characterizes throughput/latency/failure-mode only. All load rows cleaned up; cluster left healthy (`/ready` 200, DB back to baseline).

## Supplement · single-DB **multi-org isolation** verification on Postgres

The main sweep exercised the deployment under `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated` but did not carry a dedicated tenant-isolation enforcement matrix. This supplement targets that gap directly — the isolation boundary itself, on **Postgres 16.15**, against a **single shared database** in multi-org mode. All four cases **PASS**.

### Enforcement point (established first)
The isolation boundary is **application-layer** (`WHERE organization_id = <session org>` on every data-path query), **not** native Postgres row-level security. Confirmed on the live DB: `pg_policies` → **0** rows, `pg_class where relrowsecurity` → **0** tables. So these tests exercise the code path that actually enforces tenancy, not a DB feature that isn't in use.

### Method
Two real users (`owner@cluster.test`, member of both orgs `acme`/`globex`; `alice@cluster.test`, `acme`-only), driving one replica directly (`docker exec`), object `qa_iso` (`sharingModel: public_read_write` — the *most* permissive OWD, so any leak is attributable to tenancy, not record sharing), fields: `anum` (autonumber), `ucode` (unique text), `tag`. Server-truth oracles (HTTP status + persisted `organization_id`), each case run twice.

| # | case | result |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | **Forged cross-org read by id** — create record in `acme`, switch same session to `globex`, `GET /data/qa_iso/{id}` | **PASS** — `404` (isolated); the row is invisible outside its owning org even by direct id |
| T2 | **Cross-org write stamp** — `acme` session `POST` with `organization_id: <globex>` in the body | **PASS** — `201`, persisted `organization_id` = **acme**; body-supplied org **ignored**, re-stamped to session org (no write into a foreign tenant) |
| T3 | **Unique-constraint tenant scope** — same `ucode` created in `acme` then `globex` | **PASS** — both `201`; uniqueness is **per-org**, not a global index (no cross-tenant coupling / no enumeration oracle) |
| T4 | **Autonumber under multi-org (#8686)** — two creates in each org, compare `anum` | **PASS** — `acme: 0009,0010` · `globex: 0005,0006`, all distinct; **single global counter**, no per-org counter collision (the #8686 failure mode does **not** reproduce here) |

### Read this against #13331
This confirms the **data plane** isolates correctly per org on Postgres. It does **not** revisit the separate, already-filed **metadata-read** org-scope gap from the main sweep (`/meta/:type/:name/history`·`/diff`·single-item `dashboard` overlay reading env-wide under `isolated`) — that is a distinct read path and remains as extracted. Record-level tenant isolation and metadata-read org-scoping are two different enforcement points; this supplement closes the former.

Environment otherwise identical to the run above (EE 4.1.1 / runtime 17.2.0, framework `502ff8b5`, 3 replicas behind Traefik, single Postgres + Redis, isolated posture). Test object/rows cleaned up after the run.
